supplier_public_sections.text:
Adopt as a physical postulate of this framework the following four equations for
the fields of [[def-em-fields]] and the sources of [[def-em-sources]] on the
laboratory region $U\cong I\times\Omega$ of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], with
$\mu_0>0$, $c>0$, $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ and the SI units of
[[def-em-si-conventions]].

(a) [Smooth branch] Let $E,B$ be jointly $C^1$ fields with the additional
derivatives required by each equation existing and continuous, and let
$\rho,J$ be continuous. Then, with the divergence and curl of
[[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] and the partial derivative
$\partial_t$ at fixed position of
[[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]],

$$\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0,\qquad \operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB,\qquad \operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE.$$

(b) [Weak branch] Let instead $E,B$ be locally integrable $\mathbb R^3$-valued
fields and $\rho,J$ locally integrable scalar and vector fields on
$I\times\Omega$, identified with their regular distributions
([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]],
[[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]). Let
$\operatorname{div}$, $\operatorname{curl}$ and $\partial_t$ act as
distributional derivatives, componentwise, and let $\psi$ range over
$C_c^\infty(I\times\Omega)$ ([[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]]).
Then the same four identities hold in the sense of [[def-distribution]]: the
pairings

$$\langle\operatorname{div}E-\rho/\varepsilon_0,\psi\rangle,\qquad \langle\operatorname{div}B,\psi\rangle,\qquad \langle\operatorname{curl}E+\partial_tB,\psi\rangle,\qquad \langle\operatorname{curl}B-\mu_0J-c^{-2}\partial_tE,\psi\rangle$$

all vanish for every such $\psi$, all derivatives being distributional
derivatives ([[def-distributional-derivative]]).

(c) [Scope] The postulate contains no magnetic charge: $\operatorname{div}B=0$
and no magnetic-source term appears in $\operatorname{curl}E$. Sources that
are not locally integrable functions (point or sheet sources) are covered by
neither branch and require their own definition. The equations are adopted
classical vacuum physics in the named inertial chart; they are not deduced from
charge conservation, from empirical agreement or from the special-relativity
postulates, and this item by itself asserts no covariance under changes of
inertial frame.

consumer_numbered_argument.text: In the smooth branch, the identity $\operatorname{div}(\operatorname{curl}B)=0$ holds pointwise. Taking the divergence of the Ampere equation and using linearity of the coordinate derivatives gives $0=\operatorname{div}(\operatorname{curl}B)=\mu_0\operatorname{div}J+c^{-2}\operatorname{div}(\partial_tE)$, and the mixed partials commute, so $\operatorname{div}(\partial_tE)=\partial_t(\operatorname{div}E)$; the Gauss law gives $\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0$ and, $\rho$ being $C^1$, $\partial_t(\operatorname{div}E)=\varepsilon_0^{-1}\partial_t\rho$. Substituting gives $0=\mu_0\operatorname{div}J+c^{-2}\varepsilon_0^{-1}\partial_t\rho=\mu_0(\operatorname{div}J+\partial_t\rho)$, because $c^2\varepsilon_0\mu_0=1$ by the definition of $\varepsilon_0$, and division by $\mu_0>0$ gives $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$ pointwise on $\Omega\times I$. consumer_numbered_argument.text: In the distributional branch, fix $\psi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega\times I)$. The distributional curl is built from the components $\partial_jB_k-\partial_kB_j$, so $\langle\operatorname{div}(\operatorname{curl}B),\psi\rangle=\sum_{i,j,k}\varepsilon_{ijk}\langle\partial_i\partial_jB_k,\psi\rangle$, a finite sum over three indices; the distributional derivatives commute and $\varepsilon_{ijk}$ is antisymmetric, so exchanging the summation indices $i$ and $j$ presents this number as its own negative, and hence it is zero. As $\psi$ was arbitrary, $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$ in $\mathcal D'(\Omega\times I)$; every ingredient is either a distributional identity or a constant multiple, so no choice principle is used. supplier_public_sections.text:
Let the laboratory region $U\cong I\times\Omega$, its spatial Euclidean structure
and its units be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] and
[[def-em-si-conventions]], and let $k\ge1$. An **electric field of class
$C^k$** on the region is a map $E:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ that is of class
$C^k$ in the sense of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]; a
**magnetic field of class $C^k$** is a map $B:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ of
the same class. At fixed $t\in I$ the maps $E(\cdot,t),B(\cdot,t):\Omega\to
\mathbb R^3$ are real spatial vector fields on the region $\Omega$, read in the
$\delta$-orthonormal basis $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of the frame. The framework uses:
$C^1$ fields in the classical Maxwell branch, $C^2$ fields where second or
mixed time-space derivatives of the fields appear, and $C^\infty$ fields in
the smooth existence branches; every statement carries its own regularity and
no regularity beyond it is asserted.

Conventions:

(a) $E$ is a **polar vector** and $B$ an **axial vector** relative to the
orientation of the spatial basis; the changes of inertial description adopted
for this framework are proper and orientation preserving, so
orientation-reversing descriptions are not among them.

(b) The fields are defined by their values on $\Omega\times I$, and no value at
a point of singular source support is asserted.

(c) $E$ carries V m$^{-1}$ and $B$ carries T.

(d) The identification of the pair $(E,B)$ with the components of an
alternating two-form, including its transformation behaviour, is made in the
framework's electromagnetic two-form definition on this page and is not
presupposed here.

consumer_public_declarations.text:
Let $U\cong I\times\Omega$ be the laboratory region of
[[def-em-lab-geometry]], with nonempty open time interval $I$
([[def-interval]]), positive constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]] and
$\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$. Define the **Gauss defects**

$$D_B:=\operatorname{div}B,\qquad D_E:=\operatorname{div}E-\rho/\varepsilon_0.$$

(a) [Smooth evolution branch] Let $E,B$ be jointly $C^2$ fields and $\rho,J$
$C^1$ source fields of [[def-em-fields]] and [[def-em-sources]]. Assume only
the two evolution equations

$$\partial_tB=-\operatorname{curl}E,\qquad\partial_tE=c^2\operatorname{curl}B-c^2\mu_0J,$$

and, separately, source continuity $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$. No
Gauss constraint is assumed. Then $\partial_tD_B=\partial_tD_E=0$ pointwise.
For each fixed $x$, both defects are constant on $I$. Initial zero constraints
at any $t_0\in I$ persist at every time; a nonzero defect at a point persists
with the same value. Thus evolution and continuity cannot repair a nonzero
initial Gauss defect.

(b) [Distributional evolution branch] The same derivative conclusion holds for
arbitrary scalar and vector distributions $E,B,\rho,J$ on $U$ satisfying the
two evolution identities and, independently, continuity in
$\mathcal D'(U)$ ([[def-distribution]], [[def-distributional-derivative]]).
This includes the original locally integrable field and source branch
identified with regular distributions and the declared singular-source class
when its equations hold. Thus $\partial_tD_B=\partial_tD_E=0$
distributionally. If a defect has a continuous representative $h$ on $U$,
assume Countable Choice for the indicated Lebesgue integral and localization
interface ([[def-countable-choice]]); then $h(x,t)$ is independent of $t$. In
this continuous-representative case its zero or nonzero value at a time
persists. No restriction of an arbitrary distribution to a time slice is
assumed.

(c) [Full-Maxwell corollaries] Smooth solutions of
[[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] satisfy the evolution and source-continuity
hypotheses by [[pthm-em-charge-continuity]](a), and their Gauss defects are
identically zero by the two Gauss equations. Its original locally integrable
weak branch has the same distributional conclusion. For admitted point and
stationary-sheet models under [[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]],
[[pthm-em-charge-continuity]](b) supplies compatibility and the four
identities again give zero defects. Conversely, in (a), or in (b) when both
defects have continuous representatives, evolution plus continuity and zero
Gauss defects at one time give all four Maxwell identities on $U$, pointwise
in (a) and distributionally in (b).

This theorem is conditional on the stated equations and regularity. It proves
no existence, matter dynamics, observation or empirical fact. The derivative
algebra is choice-free; Countable Choice is confined to the
continuous-representative localization and the inherited declared
singular-source formulation.

consumer_numbered_argument.text: For the continuous-representative statement assume $\partial_th=0$ in $\mathcal D'(U)$ for a continuous $h$, and let $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$. The function $F(t):=\int_\Omega h(x,t)\varphi(x)\,d\lambda_3(x)$ is continuous on $I$: on a compact time interval the integrands have the fixed compact spatial support of $\varphi$ and a uniform bound coming from continuity of $h$ on the compact set $\operatorname{supp}\varphi\times$ that interval, so dominated convergence applies. For $\eta\in C_c^\infty(I)$ with $\int_I\eta=0$, extend $\eta$ by zero and put $H(t):=\int_{-\infty}^t\eta(v)\,dv$; the FTC makes $H$ smooth with $H'=\eta$, and $H$ vanishes off the support of $\eta$, so $\Psi(x,t):=\varphi(x)H(t)$ is a compact smooth test with $\partial_t\Psi=\varphi\eta$; applying the derivative equation to this primitive test gives $0=\langle\partial_th,\Psi\rangle=-\langle h,\partial_t\Psi\rangle=-\int_IF(t)\eta(t)\,dt$, the multiple integral being identified with the iterated one by the Borel product structure and Fubini and its Riemann-Lebesgue value by the comparison lemma. Choosing a nonnegative compact bump $\beta$ of integral one and writing an arbitrary temporal test as $\eta=\eta_0+(\int_I\eta)\beta$ with $\int_I\eta_0=0$ gives $\int_I(F-C)\eta_0=0$ for all $\eta_0$ with zero integral and $C:=\int_IF\beta$; since also $\int_I(F-C)\beta=\int_IF\beta-C\int_I\beta=0$, every $\eta\in C_c^\infty(I)$ satisfies $\int_I(F-C)\eta=0$, and the sign-and-bump argument (a nonzero value of the continuous $F-C$ at a point persists with one sign on a subinterval of positive measure, and a nonnegative bump equal to one on a smaller subinterval has strictly nonzero pairing by monotonicity and the positive finite measure of that subinterval) then forces $F-C=0$, that is, $F=C$ constant on $I$. Since $\varphi$ is arbitrary, $h(\cdot,t_1)-h(\cdot,t_2)$ is a continuous function on $\Omega$ whose pairing against every spatial test vanishes, so the same sign-and-bump argument in $\mathbb R^3$ gives $h(\cdot,t_1)=h(\cdot,t_2)$; hence $h$ is independent of $t$. [F4, F6, given, algebra]

supplier_public_sections.text:
Adopt the SI system of units for this framework, with the following quantity
table and conventions; every symbol is a quantity of this framework and the
laboratory structure is that of [[def-em-lab-geometry]].

(a) [Coordinates and constants] $x^0=ct$ and each spatial coordinate $x^i$
carries the metre (m); the time coordinate $t$ carries the second (s); the
conversion constant $c>0$ carries m s$^{-1}$ and has the exact SI defining
value $c=299\,792\,458\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$; the elementary charge $e$ has the
exact SI defining value $e=1.602\,176\,634\times10^{-19}\ \mathrm{C}$, and this
item does not assert that physical charge is quantised; the magnetic constant
$\mu_0>0$ carries N A$^{-2}$ and is measured, so no exact numerical value of
$\mu_0$ is asserted. The pre-2019 SI fixed the historical nominal
$\mu_{0,\mathrm{nom}}:=4\pi\times10^{-7}\ \mathrm{H\,m^{-1}}
=4\pi\times10^{-7}\ \mathrm{N\,A^{-2}}$ exactly; since the revised SI took
effect on 20 May 2019, $\mu_0$ is experimentally determined. The SI brochure
quotes the nominal $\mu_{0,\mathrm{nom}}$ as the estimate at the 2019 adoption
with relative standard uncertainty $2.3\times10^{-10}$; this is historical
estimate and uncertainty context, not an exact equality for the actual $\mu_0$
or a current measured value. The electric constant is defined within the
framework by

$$\varepsilon_0:=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$$

in F m$^{-1}$, consistent with the exact SI relation $\varepsilon_0\mu_0=1/c^2$,
so that $c^2\varepsilon_0\mu_0=1$ and $\varepsilon_0$ inherits the relative
standard uncertainty of $\mu_0$.

(b) [Electromagnetic quantities] Charge $q$ carries the coulomb (C); the
charge density $\rho$ of the framework's source definition carries C m$^{-3}$
and the current density $J$ carries A m$^{-2}$, so that the four-current
components $(c\rho,J)$ carry A m$^{-2}$; the electric field $E$ carries
V m$^{-1}$; the magnetic field $B$ carries the tesla (T), where
$1\ \mathrm{T}=1\ \mathrm{N\,A^{-1}\,m^{-1}}$; the scalar potential $\varphi$
carries V and the vector potential $A$ carries T m, so that the four-potential
components $(\varphi/c,A)$ carry T m; the components of the electromagnetic
two-form of the framework's tensor definition carry T; a force carries the
newton (N), $1\ \mathrm{N}=1\ \mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-2}}$.

(c) [Mechanical quantities] A rest mass parameter $m$ carries the kilogram
(kg) and a four-momentum $P=mU$ of the relativistic particle model carries
kg m s$^{-1}$; field energy density carries J m$^{-3}$, energy flux
W m$^{-2}$, so that $1\ \mathrm{W}=1\ \mathrm{J\,s^{-1}}=1\ \mathrm{V\,A}$.

(d) [Bookkeeping only] The unit of a quantity records the adopted system of
units; it does not show that a quantity is primitive in this or any other
framework, it contains no measurement, and it does not identify a quantity
with a similarly named quantity of another framework. The exact defining
values of $c$ and $e$ fix numerical conventions of the SI; they do not by
themselves identify $c$ with the vacuum propagation constant of ideal light,
which is the physical adoption of the framework's Minkowski postulate.

(a) [Smooth evolution branch] Let $E,B$ be jointly $C^2$ fields and $\rho,J$
$C^1$ source fields of [[def-em-fields]] and [[def-em-sources]]. Assume only
the two evolution equations

$$\partial_tB=-\operatorname{curl}E,\qquad\partial_tE=c^2\operatorname{curl}B-c^2\mu_0J,$$

and, separately, source continuity $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$. No
Gauss constraint is assumed. Then $\partial_tD_B=\partial_tD_E=0$ pointwise.
For each fixed $x$, both defects are constant on $I$. Initial zero constraints
at any $t_0\in I$ persist at every time; a nonzero defect at a point persists
with the same value. Thus evolution and continuity cannot repair a nonzero
initial Gauss defect.

(b) [Distributional evolution branch] The same derivative conclusion holds for
arbitrary scalar and vector distributions $E,B,\rho,J$ on $U$ satisfying the
two evolution identities and, independently, continuity in
$\mathcal D'(U)$ ([[def-distribution]], [[def-distributional-derivative]]).
This includes the original locally integrable field and source branch
identified with regular distributions and the declared singular-source class
when its equations hold. Thus $\partial_tD_B=\partial_tD_E=0$
distributionally. If a defect has a continuous representative $h$ on $U$,
assume Countable Choice for the indicated Lebesgue integral and localization
interface ([[def-countable-choice]]); then $h(x,t)$ is independent of $t$. In
this continuous-representative case its zero or nonzero value at a time
persists. No restriction of an arbitrary distribution to a time slice is
assumed.

(c) [Full-Maxwell corollaries] Smooth solutions of
[[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] satisfy the evolution and source-continuity
hypotheses by [[pthm-em-charge-continuity]](a), and their Gauss defects are
identically zero by the two Gauss equations. Its original locally integrable
weak branch has the same distributional conclusion. For admitted point and
stationary-sheet models under [[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]],
[[pthm-em-charge-continuity]](b) supplies compatibility and the four
identities again give zero defects. Conversely, in (a), or in (b) when both
defects have continuous representatives, evolution plus continuity and zero
Gauss defects at one time give all four Maxwell identities on $U$, pointwise
in (a) and distributionally in (b).

This theorem is conditional on the stated equations and regularity. It proves

continuous-representative localization and the inherited declared
singular-source formulation.

supplier_public_sections.text:
Let the laboratory region and its chart be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], with
the units of [[def-em-si-conventions]].

(a) [Charge parameter] The framework takes a real **charge parameter**
$q\in\mathbb R$, measured in coulombs, attached to a source; its sign is the
sign of the source and it is a parameter of the model. Charge quantisation is
not asserted.

(b) [Smooth source fields] A **smooth (volume) source field** on
$\Omega\times I$ is a pair $(\rho,J)$ of maps $\rho:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R$,
$J:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ that is continuous on $\Omega\times I$ and of
class $C^1$ wherever a displayed equation differentiates it; $\rho$ is the
**frame charge density** (C m$^{-3}$) and $J$ the **frame current density**
(A m$^{-2}$). For each fixed $t\in I$ retain the compact Jordan branch: if
$V\subseteq\Omega$ is compact and Jordan measurable, define

$$Q_R(V,t):=\int_V\rho(y,t)dy$$

by [[def-riemann-integral-over-a-jordan-set]], with integrability supplied by
[[thm-continuous-functions-on-compact-jordan-sets-are-integrable]]. For the
full measurable-volume branch assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]),
as required by the published Lebesgue-measure interface. If $V$ is any bounded
Lebesgue-measurable subset with compact closure $\overline V\subseteq\Omega$,
define

$$Q(V,t):=\int_V\rho(y,t)d\lambda_3(y)=\int_{\mathbb R^3}F_t(y)\mathbf{1}_V(y)d\lambda_3(y),$$

where $F_t=\rho(\cdot,t)$ on $\Omega$ and $0$ elsewhere; the signed integral is
defined through its positive and negative parts
([[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]],
[[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]]). The
function $F_t$ is Borel, and hence Lebesgue measurable: for every open
$O\subseteq\mathbb R$ its preimage inside the open set $\Omega$ is relatively
open in $\Omega$, hence open in $\mathbb R^3$, and the closed complement of
$\Omega$ is added precisely when $0\in O$
([[thm-continuous-preimages-of-borel-sets-are-borel]],
[[thm-borel-sets-are-lebesgue-measurable]]). This integral is absolutely
finite: $\rho(\cdot,t)$ is bounded on the compact $\overline V$ by
[[thm-extreme-value-metric]], $V$ has finite Lebesgue measure by
[[prop-lebesgue-measure-is-sigma-finite-and-finite-on-bounded-sets]], and the
monotonicity and homogeneity of the nonnegative integral
([[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]) bound
$\int|F_t|\mathbf{1}_Vd\lambda_3\le M_t\lambda_3(V)<\infty$, the indicator
integral being its simple-function value
([[prop-the-nonnegative-integral-agrees-with-the-simple-integral]]); the
positive and negative parts are measurable by
[[prop-closure-properties-of-measurable-functions-used-by-the-integral]]. On
the compact Jordan branch, under the same Countable Choice assumption,
$Q=Q_R$ by [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]].
The
empty region has charge zero in both branches. The current flux remains
defined independently: for each oriented surface patch in $\Omega$ the current
flux at time $t$ is the surface integral of $J(\cdot,t)$ in the induced
orientation, as defined in [[def-oriented-unit-normal-and-flux-of-a-surface-patch]].
Point sources and sheet sources are not source fields in this sense; they are
different objects, defined by their own pairings when the framework uses them.

(c) [Covariant identification] Write $j:=(c\rho,J)$, so $j^0=c\rho$ and
$j^i=J^i$. The framework adopts as a model premise the identification of the
charge-current of a source with a vector field of the affine Minkowski model,
and hence the component transformation law of
[[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] for $j$ between inertial charts.
This is a model premise, not a theorem about physical currents.

(d) [Frame density, scalar multiplier and the normalized material branch]
Suppose additionally that the identified $j$ is $C^1$ and $j=\rho_0U$, with a
$C^1$ future timelike vector field $U$ and a $C^1$ real scalar multiplier
$\rho_0$. Since $U^0>0$, define the normalized chart direction $u:=U/U^0$, so
$u^0=1$, $u^i=U^i/U^0$. Then $j=(\rho_0U^0)u$ and, because the electromagnetic
convention is $j^0=c\rho$,

$$\rho=\rho_0U^0/c,\qquad J^i=\rho_0U^i=c\rho\,u^i.$$

Pointwise equality $\rho=\rho_0$ holds if and only if $\rho_0(U^0-c)=0$,
including the zero-multiplier case. Where $\rho_0\ne0$, equality is equivalent
to $U^0=c$, which does not alone imply $U^i=0$ for an arbitrary future timelike
$U$. Thus a scalar multiplier is not automatically a Lorentz rest charge
density. The direction $u$ is chart normalized, with no unit or
proper-four-velocity normalization imposed in this general branch; if its
coordinate velocity interpretation is adopted, the spatial velocity is
$v^i:=cu^i$.

For the separate convective source model, explicitly assume that $U$ is the
material proper-time four-velocity, normalized by $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$ as in
[[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]. This is an additional model
condition, not a consequence of the factorization $j=\rho_0U$. In that branch,
$U=\gamma(c,v)$, $|v|<c$, $\gamma=(1-|v|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$, and

$$\rho=\gamma\rho_0,\qquad J=\rho v.$$

Here $\rho_0$ is the rest charge density of this stipulated convective model:
in a comoving inertial frame $U=(c,0,0,0)$ and $j=(c\rho_0,0,0,0)$. The
equality $\rho=\rho_0$ then holds exactly where $\rho_0=0$ or $v=0$
(equivalently $\gamma=1$). Both signs of charge and the zero-density case are
retained.

(e) [Scope] This definition fixes the source objects of the smooth branch and
their transformation interface. It asserts no conservation law (that is proved
for stated source classes) and no regularity of singular sources.

The function $F(t):=\int_\Omega h(x,t)\varphi(x)\,d\lambda_3(x)$ is continuous on $I$: on a compact time interval the integrands have the fixed compact spatial support of $\varphi$ and a uniform bound coming from continuity of $h$ on the compact set $\operatorname{supp}\varphi\times$ that interval, so dominated convergence applies. For $\eta\in C_c^\infty(I)$ with $\int_I\eta=0$, extend $\eta$ by zero and put $H(t):=\int_{-\infty}^t\eta(v)\,dv$; the FTC makes $H$ smooth with $H'=\eta$, and $H$ vanishes off the support of $\eta$, so $\Psi(x,t):=\varphi(x)H(t)$ is a compact smooth test with $\partial_t\Psi=\varphi\eta$; applying the derivative equation to this primitive test gives $0=\langle\partial_th,\Psi\rangle=-\langle h,\partial_t\Psi\rangle=-\int_IF(t)\eta(t)\,dt$, the multiple integral being identified with the iterated one by the Borel product structure and Fubini and its Riemann-Lebesgue value by the comparison lemma. Choosing a nonnegative compact bump $\beta$ of integral one and writing an arbitrary temporal test as $\eta=\eta_0+(\int_I\eta)\beta$ with $\int_I\eta_0=0$ gives $\int_I(F-C)\eta_0=0$ for all $\eta_0$ with zero integral and $C:=\int_IF\beta$; since also $\int_I(F-C)\beta=\int_IF\beta-C\int_I\beta=0$, every $\eta\in C_c^\infty(I)$ satisfies $\int_I(F-C)\eta=0$, and the sign-and-bump argument (a nonzero value of the continuous $F-C$ at a point persists with one sign on a subinterval of positive measure, and a nonnegative bump equal to one on a smaller subinterval has strictly nonzero pairing by monotonicity and the positive finite measure of that subinterval) then forces $F-C=0$, that is, $F=C$ constant on $I$. Since $\varphi$ is arbitrary, $h(\cdot,t_1)-h(\cdot,t_2)$ is a continuous function on $\Omega$ whose pairing against every spatial test vanishes, so the same sign-and-bump argument in $\mathbb R^3$ gives $h(\cdot,t_1)=h(\cdot,t_2)$; hence $h$ is independent of $t$. supplier_public_sections.text:
Adopt as a physical postulate of this framework the following four equations for
the fields of [[def-em-fields]] and the sources of [[def-em-sources]] on the
laboratory region $U\cong I\times\Omega$ of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], with
$\mu_0>0$, $c>0$, $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ and the SI units of
[[def-em-si-conventions]].

(a) [Smooth branch] Let $E,B$ be jointly $C^1$ fields with the additional
derivatives required by each equation existing and continuous, and let
$\rho,J$ be continuous. Then, with the divergence and curl of
[[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] and the partial derivative
$\partial_t$ at fixed position of
[[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]],

$$\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0,\qquad \operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB,\qquad \operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE.$$

(b) [Weak branch] Let instead $E,B$ be locally integrable $\mathbb R^3$-valued
fields and $\rho,J$ locally integrable scalar and vector fields on
$I\times\Omega$, identified with their regular distributions
([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]],
[[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]). Let
$\operatorname{div}$, $\operatorname{curl}$ and $\partial_t$ act as
distributional derivatives, componentwise, and let $\psi$ range over
$C_c^\infty(I\times\Omega)$ ([[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]]).
Then the same four identities hold in the sense of [[def-distribution]]: the
pairings

$$\langle\operatorname{div}E-\rho/\varepsilon_0,\psi\rangle,\qquad \langle\operatorname{div}B,\psi\rangle,\qquad \langle\operatorname{curl}E+\partial_tB,\psi\rangle,\qquad \langle\operatorname{curl}B-\mu_0J-c^{-2}\partial_tE,\psi\rangle$$

all vanish for every such $\psi$, all derivatives being distributional
derivatives ([[def-distributional-derivative]]).

(c) [Scope] The postulate contains no magnetic charge: $\operatorname{div}B=0$
and no magnetic-source term appears in $\operatorname{curl}E$. Sources that
are not locally integrable functions (point or sheet sources) are covered by
neither branch and require their own definition. The equations are adopted
classical vacuum physics in the named inertial chart; they are not deduced from
charge conservation, from empirical agreement or from the special-relativity
postulates, and this item by itself asserts no covariance under changes of
inertial frame.

consumer_public_declarations.text:
Let $U\cong I\times\Omega$ be the laboratory region of
[[def-em-lab-geometry]], with nonempty open time interval $I$
([[def-interval]]), positive constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]] and
$\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$. Define the **Gauss defects**

$$D_B:=\operatorname{div}B,\qquad D_E:=\operatorname{div}E-\rho/\varepsilon_0.$$

(a) [Smooth evolution branch] Let $E,B$ be jointly $C^2$ fields and $\rho,J$
$C^1$ source fields of [[def-em-fields]] and [[def-em-sources]]. Assume only
the two evolution equations

$$\partial_tB=-\operatorname{curl}E,\qquad\partial_tE=c^2\operatorname{curl}B-c^2\mu_0J,$$

and, separately, source continuity $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$. No
Gauss constraint is assumed. Then $\partial_tD_B=\partial_tD_E=0$ pointwise.
For each fixed $x$, both defects are constant on $I$. Initial zero constraints
at any $t_0\in I$ persist at every time; a nonzero defect at a point persists
with the same value. Thus evolution and continuity cannot repair a nonzero
initial Gauss defect.

(b) [Distributional evolution branch] The same derivative conclusion holds for
arbitrary scalar and vector distributions $E,B,\rho,J$ on $U$ satisfying the
two evolution identities and, independently, continuity in
$\mathcal D'(U)$ ([[def-distribution]], [[def-distributional-derivative]]).
This includes the original locally integrable field and source branch
identified with regular distributions and the declared singular-source class
when its equations hold. Thus $\partial_tD_B=\partial_tD_E=0$
distributionally. If a defect has a continuous representative $h$ on $U$,
assume Countable Choice for the indicated Lebesgue integral and localization
interface ([[def-countable-choice]]); then $h(x,t)$ is independent of $t$. In
this continuous-representative case its zero or nonzero value at a time
persists. No restriction of an arbitrary distribution to a time slice is
assumed.

(c) [Full-Maxwell corollaries] Smooth solutions of
[[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] satisfy the evolution and source-continuity
hypotheses by [[pthm-em-charge-continuity]](a), and their Gauss defects are
identically zero by the two Gauss equations. Its original locally integrable
weak branch has the same distributional conclusion. For admitted point and
stationary-sheet models under [[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]],
[[pthm-em-charge-continuity]](b) supplies compatibility and the four
identities again give zero defects. Conversely, in (a), or in (b) when both
defects have continuous representatives, evolution plus continuity and zero
Gauss defects at one time give all four Maxwell identities on $U$, pointwise
in (a) and distributionally in (b).

This theorem is conditional on the stated equations and regularity. It proves
no existence, matter dynamics, observation or empirical fact. The derivative
algebra is choice-free; Countable Choice is confined to the
continuous-representative localization and the inherited declared
singular-source formulation.

supplier_public_sections.text:
Let the laboratory region $U\cong I\times\Omega$, its spatial Euclidean structure
and its units be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] and
[[def-em-si-conventions]], and let $k\ge1$. An **electric field of class
$C^k$** on the region is a map $E:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ that is of class
$C^k$ in the sense of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]; a
**magnetic field of class $C^k$** is a map $B:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ of
the same class. At fixed $t\in I$ the maps $E(\cdot,t),B(\cdot,t):\Omega\to
\mathbb R^3$ are real spatial vector fields on the region $\Omega$, read in the
$\delta$-orthonormal basis $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of the frame. The framework uses:
$C^1$ fields in the classical Maxwell branch, $C^2$ fields where second or
mixed time-space derivatives of the fields appear, and $C^\infty$ fields in
the smooth existence branches; every statement carries its own regularity and
no regularity beyond it is asserted.

Conventions:

(a) $E$ is a **polar vector** and $B$ an **axial vector** relative to the
orientation of the spatial basis; the changes of inertial description adopted
for this framework are proper and orientation preserving, so
orientation-reversing descriptions are not among them.

(b) The fields are defined by their values on $\Omega\times I$, and no value at
a point of singular source support is asserted.

(c) $E$ carries V m$^{-1}$ and $B$ carries T.

(d) The identification of the pair $(E,B)$ with the components of an
alternating two-form, including its transformation behaviour, is made in the
framework's electromagnetic two-form definition on this page and is not
presupposed here.

consumer_public_declarations.text:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, the convention of the
imported piecewise $C^1$ boundary and surface-measure definitions
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $U\cong I\times\Omega$ be the laboratory region
of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] with the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]]; let
$E,B$ be fields of [[def-em-fields]] and $\rho,J$ source fields of
[[def-em-sources]] on $\Omega\times I$; and let $(V,\nu_V)$ and $(D,r)$ be the
volume and patch test geometries of [[def-em-fixed-test-geometry]]. Assume the
fields are jointly $C^1$ on $\Omega\times I$ and that the additional
derivatives appearing below exist and are continuous there; for instance $E,B$
jointly of class $C^2$ and $\rho,J$ of class $C^1$ is sufficient.

(a) [Differential implies integral] If the smooth branch of
[[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] holds pointwise on $\Omega\times I$, then for every
volume test geometry $(V,\nu_V)$ and every $t\in I$,

$$\oint_{\partial V}E(\cdot,t)\cdot\nu_V\,dS=\frac{1}{\varepsilon_0}\int_V\rho(\cdot,t)\,d\lambda_3,\qquad \oint_{\partial V}B(\cdot,t)\cdot\nu_V\,dS=0,$$

and for every patch test geometry $(D,r)$ the flux functions
$t\mapsto\int_SB(\cdot,t)\cdot n_S\,dS$ and
$t\mapsto\int_SE(\cdot,t)\cdot n_S\,dS$ are differentiable on $I$ and, for
every $t\in I$,

$$\oint_{\partial S}E(\cdot,t)\cdot d\mathbf r=-\frac{d}{dt}\int_SB(\cdot,t)\cdot n_S\,dS,\qquad \oint_{\partial S}B(\cdot,t)\cdot d\mathbf r=\mu_0\int_SJ(\cdot,t)\cdot n_S\,dS+c^{-2}\frac{d}{dt}\int_SE(\cdot,t)\cdot n_S\,dS.$$

(b) [Integral implies differential] Conversely, suppose the two volume
identities of (a) hold for every volume test geometry and every $t\in I$, and
that for every patch test geometry the two flux functions are differentiable
on $I$ and the two patch identities of (a) hold for every $t\in I$. Then the
four smooth-branch equations of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] hold pointwise on
$\Omega\times I$:

$$\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0,\qquad \operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB,\qquad \operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE.$$

The equivalence is asserted for the exact class of test geometries of
[[def-em-fixed-test-geometry]], which contains the open interiors of all closed
axis-parallel boxes compactly contained in $\Omega$ and the affine square
patches; it is not a recovery from one selected volume or one selected patch,
and the divergence and curl of
[[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] and the time derivative of
[[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]] are the operators used.

consumer_numbered_argument.text: For the patch identities of (a), fix a patch test geometry $(D,r)$ and put $S=r[D]$, with parameter derivatives $r_u,r_v$ and oriented area vector $r_u\times r_v$. The flux functions $\Phi_B(t):=\int_D\langle B(r(u,v),t),r_u(u,v)\times r_v(u,v)\rangle\,dudv$ and $\Phi_E$ are differentiable on $I$ with $\Phi_B'(t)=\int_S\partial_tB(\cdot,t)\cdot n_S\,dS$ and $\Phi_E'(t)=\int_S\partial_tE(\cdot,t)\cdot n_S\,dS$: the integrands are the continuous functions $\langle B(r(u,v),t),r_u\times r_v\rangle$ with continuous $t$-derivative $\langle\partial_tB(r(u,v),t),r_u\times r_v\rangle$ on a neighbourhood of the compact Jordan region $D$ times a compact interval around $t$, [F6] identifies the Riemann integral with the Lebesgue integral, and [F7] differentiates under the integral. Stokes' theorem [F5] applied to the $C^1$ fields gives $\oint_{\partial S}E(\cdot,t)\cdot d\mathbf r=\int_S\operatorname{curl}E(\cdot,t)\cdot n_S\,dS$ and the corresponding identity for $B$, in the induced orientation of the patch; substituting the Faraday law $\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$ of [F1] gives $\oint_{\partial S}E(\cdot,t)\cdot d\mathbf r=-\int_S\partial_tB(\cdot,t)\cdot n_S\,dS=-\Phi_B'(t)$, and substituting the Ampere law gives $\oint_{\partial S}B(\cdot,t)\cdot d\mathbf r=\mu_0\int_SJ(\cdot,t)\cdot n_S\,dS+c^{-2}\Phi_E'(t)$. [F1, F2, F5, F6, F7, given, algebra]

consumer_numbered_argument.text: For clause (b), fix a closed axis-parallel box $K=\prod_{i<3}[a_i,b_i]\subseteq\Omega$ with $a_i<b_i$ and let $V$ be its open interior, a volume test geometry with $\overline V=K$ by [F2]. The volume identity hypothesis and the divergence theorem give $0=\oint_{\partial V}E(\cdot,t)\cdot\nu_V\,dS-(1/\varepsilon_0)\int_V\rho(\cdot,t)\,d\lambda_3=\int_Vh\,d\lambda_3$ for the continuous function $h:=\operatorname{div}E-\rho/\varepsilon_0$, where linearity [F9] combines the two finite integrals and [F4] identifies the flux with $\int_V\operatorname{div}E$; by [F2] and [F9] this equals $\int_Kh\,d\lambda_3$, because $K\setminus V$ is $\lambda_3$-null. Since every closed axis-parallel box $K\subseteq\Omega$ with positive sides arises this way, [F8] with $n=3$ gives $h=0$ on $\Omega$, that is $\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0$. The same computation with the second volume identity and $\int_V\operatorname{div}B=0$ gives $\operatorname{div}B=0$. [F1, F2, F4, F8, F9, given, algebra]

consumer_numbered_argument.text: For the curl equations fix a point $p\in\Omega$ and let $(j,k)$ be the cyclic pair with $e_j\times e_k=e_i$ for a coordinate index $i$. Put $W:=\{(u,v)\in\mathbb R^2:p+ue_j+ve_k\in\Omega\}$, an open set, and $\varphi_i(u,v):=\bigl(\operatorname{curl}E+\partial_tB\bigr)(p+ue_j+ve_k)\cdot e_i$ on $W$, a continuous function. For every closed axis-parallel square $Q\subseteq W$ with side $\ell>0$ the affine patch $r(u,v):=p+ue_j+ve_k$ over $Q$ is a patch test geometry with $r_u\times r_v=e_i$ and image in $\Omega$; Stokes [F5], the differentiability of its flux function and the Faraday identity of the hypothesis give $\int_Q\varphi_i\,dudv=\int_Q\langle(\operatorname{curl}E)\circ r,r_u\times r_v\rangle\,dudv+\frac{d}{dt}\int_Q\langle B\circ r,r_u\times r_v\rangle\,dudv=\oint_{\partial S}E\cdot d\mathbf r+\frac{d}{dt}\int_SB\cdot n_S\,dS=0$. Hence the continuous function $\varphi_i$ has vanishing integral over every closed axis-parallel square contained in $W$, so the planar clause of [F8] gives $\varphi_i=0$ on $W$. The point $p\in\Omega$ was chosen arbitrarily, and $(0,0)\in W$ because $p\in\Omega$, so evaluating at $(0,0)$ gives $(\operatorname{curl}E+\partial_tB)(p)\cdot e_i=0$ for every $p\in\Omega$; letting $i$ run over the three coordinate indices, $\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$ on $\Omega$. The same argument with the Ampere identity in place of Faraday gives $\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$, the flux derivative producing $c^{-2}\Phi_E'$. [F2, F3, F5, F6, F7, F8, given, algebra]

supplier_public_sections.text:
Adopt the SI system of units for this framework, with the following quantity
table and conventions; every symbol is a quantity of this framework and the
laboratory structure is that of [[def-em-lab-geometry]].

(a) [Coordinates and constants] $x^0=ct$ and each spatial coordinate $x^i$
carries the metre (m); the time coordinate $t$ carries the second (s); the
conversion constant $c>0$ carries m s$^{-1}$ and has the exact SI defining
value $c=299\,792\,458\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$; the elementary charge $e$ has the
exact SI defining value $e=1.602\,176\,634\times10^{-19}\ \mathrm{C}$, and this
item does not assert that physical charge is quantised; the magnetic constant
$\mu_0>0$ carries N A$^{-2}$ and is measured, so no exact numerical value of
$\mu_0$ is asserted. The pre-2019 SI fixed the historical nominal
$\mu_{0,\mathrm{nom}}:=4\pi\times10^{-7}\ \mathrm{H\,m^{-1}}
=4\pi\times10^{-7}\ \mathrm{N\,A^{-2}}$ exactly; since the revised SI took
effect on 20 May 2019, $\mu_0$ is experimentally determined. The SI brochure
quotes the nominal $\mu_{0,\mathrm{nom}}$ as the estimate at the 2019 adoption
with relative standard uncertainty $2.3\times10^{-10}$; this is historical
estimate and uncertainty context, not an exact equality for the actual $\mu_0$
or a current measured value. The electric constant is defined within the
framework by

$$\varepsilon_0:=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$$

in F m$^{-1}$, consistent with the exact SI relation $\varepsilon_0\mu_0=1/c^2$,
so that $c^2\varepsilon_0\mu_0=1$ and $\varepsilon_0$ inherits the relative
standard uncertainty of $\mu_0$.

(b) [Electromagnetic quantities] Charge $q$ carries the coulomb (C); the
charge density $\rho$ of the framework's source definition carries C m$^{-3}$
and the current density $J$ carries A m$^{-2}$, so that the four-current
components $(c\rho,J)$ carry A m$^{-2}$; the electric field $E$ carries
V m$^{-1}$; the magnetic field $B$ carries the tesla (T), where
$1\ \mathrm{T}=1\ \mathrm{N\,A^{-1}\,m^{-1}}$; the scalar potential $\varphi$
carries V and the vector potential $A$ carries T m, so that the four-potential
components $(\varphi/c,A)$ carry T m; the components of the electromagnetic
two-form of the framework's tensor definition carry T; a force carries the
newton (N), $1\ \mathrm{N}=1\ \mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-2}}$.

(c) [Mechanical quantities] A rest mass parameter $m$ carries the kilogram
(kg) and a four-momentum $P=mU$ of the relativistic particle model carries
kg m s$^{-1}$; field energy density carries J m$^{-3}$, energy flux
W m$^{-2}$, so that $1\ \mathrm{W}=1\ \mathrm{J\,s^{-1}}=1\ \mathrm{V\,A}$.

(d) [Bookkeeping only] The unit of a quantity records the adopted system of
units; it does not show that a quantity is primitive in this or any other
framework, it contains no measurement, and it does not identify a quantity
with a similarly named quantity of another framework. The exact defining
values of $c$ and $e$ fix numerical conventions of the SI; they do not by
themselves identify $c$ with the vacuum propagation constant of ideal light,
which is the physical adoption of the framework's Minkowski postulate.

supplier_public_sections.text:
Let the laboratory region and its chart be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], with
the units of [[def-em-si-conventions]].

(a) [Charge parameter] The framework takes a real **charge parameter**
$q\in\mathbb R$, measured in coulombs, attached to a source; its sign is the
sign of the source and it is a parameter of the model. Charge quantisation is
not asserted.

(b) [Smooth source fields] A **smooth (volume) source field** on
$\Omega\times I$ is a pair $(\rho,J)$ of maps $\rho:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R$,
$J:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ that is continuous on $\Omega\times I$ and of
class $C^1$ wherever a displayed equation differentiates it; $\rho$ is the
**frame charge density** (C m$^{-3}$) and $J$ the **frame current density**
(A m$^{-2}$). For each fixed $t\in I$ retain the compact Jordan branch: if
$V\subseteq\Omega$ is compact and Jordan measurable, define

$$Q_R(V,t):=\int_V\rho(y,t)dy$$

by [[def-riemann-integral-over-a-jordan-set]], with integrability supplied by
[[thm-continuous-functions-on-compact-jordan-sets-are-integrable]]. For the
full measurable-volume branch assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]),
as required by the published Lebesgue-measure interface. If $V$ is any bounded
Lebesgue-measurable subset with compact closure $\overline V\subseteq\Omega$,
define

$$Q(V,t):=\int_V\rho(y,t)d\lambda_3(y)=\int_{\mathbb R^3}F_t(y)\mathbf{1}_V(y)d\lambda_3(y),$$

where $F_t=\rho(\cdot,t)$ on $\Omega$ and $0$ elsewhere; the signed integral is
defined through its positive and negative parts
([[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]],
[[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]]). The
function $F_t$ is Borel, and hence Lebesgue measurable: for every open
$O\subseteq\mathbb R$ its preimage inside the open set $\Omega$ is relatively
open in $\Omega$, hence open in $\mathbb R^3$, and the closed complement of
$\Omega$ is added precisely when $0\in O$
([[thm-continuous-preimages-of-borel-sets-are-borel]],
[[thm-borel-sets-are-lebesgue-measurable]]). This integral is absolutely
finite: $\rho(\cdot,t)$ is bounded on the compact $\overline V$ by
[[thm-extreme-value-metric]], $V$ has finite Lebesgue measure by
[[prop-lebesgue-measure-is-sigma-finite-and-finite-on-bounded-sets]], and the
monotonicity and homogeneity of the nonnegative integral
([[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]) bound
$\int|F_t|\mathbf{1}_Vd\lambda_3\le M_t\lambda_3(V)<\infty$, the indicator
integral being its simple-function value
([[prop-the-nonnegative-integral-agrees-with-the-simple-integral]]); the
positive and negative parts are measurable by
[[prop-closure-properties-of-measurable-functions-used-by-the-integral]]. On
the compact Jordan branch, under the same Countable Choice assumption,
$Q=Q_R$ by [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]].
The
empty region has charge zero in both branches. The current flux remains
defined independently: for each oriented surface patch in $\Omega$ the current
flux at time $t$ is the surface integral of $J(\cdot,t)$ in the induced
orientation, as defined in [[def-oriented-unit-normal-and-flux-of-a-surface-patch]].
Point sources and sheet sources are not source fields in this sense; they are
different objects, defined by their own pairings when the framework uses them.

(c) [Covariant identification] Write $j:=(c\rho,J)$, so $j^0=c\rho$ and
$j^i=J^i$. The framework adopts as a model premise the identification of the
charge-current of a source with a vector field of the affine Minkowski model,
and hence the component transformation law of
[[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] for $j$ between inertial charts.
This is a model premise, not a theorem about physical currents.

(d) [Frame density, scalar multiplier and the normalized material branch]
Suppose additionally that the identified $j$ is $C^1$ and $j=\rho_0U$, with a
$C^1$ future timelike vector field $U$ and a $C^1$ real scalar multiplier
$\rho_0$. Since $U^0>0$, define the normalized chart direction $u:=U/U^0$, so
$u^0=1$, $u^i=U^i/U^0$. Then $j=(\rho_0U^0)u$ and, because the electromagnetic
convention is $j^0=c\rho$,

$$\rho=\rho_0U^0/c,\qquad J^i=\rho_0U^i=c\rho\,u^i.$$

Pointwise equality $\rho=\rho_0$ holds if and only if $\rho_0(U^0-c)=0$,
including the zero-multiplier case. Where $\rho_0\ne0$, equality is equivalent
to $U^0=c$, which does not alone imply $U^i=0$ for an arbitrary future timelike
$U$. Thus a scalar multiplier is not automatically a Lorentz rest charge
density. The direction $u$ is chart normalized, with no unit or
proper-four-velocity normalization imposed in this general branch; if its
coordinate velocity interpretation is adopted, the spatial velocity is
$v^i:=cu^i$.

For the separate convective source model, explicitly assume that $U$ is the
material proper-time four-velocity, normalized by $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$ as in
[[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]. This is an additional model
condition, not a consequence of the factorization $j=\rho_0U$. In that branch,
$U=\gamma(c,v)$, $|v|<c$, $\gamma=(1-|v|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$, and

$$\rho=\gamma\rho_0,\qquad J=\rho v.$$

Here $\rho_0$ is the rest charge density of this stipulated convective model:
in a comoving inertial frame $U=(c,0,0,0)$ and $j=(c\rho_0,0,0,0)$. The
equality $\rho=\rho_0$ then holds exactly where $\rho_0=0$ or $v=0$
(equivalently $\gamma=1$). Both signs of charge and the zero-density case are
retained.

(e) [Scope] This definition fixes the source objects of the smooth branch and
their transformation interface. It asserts no conservation law (that is proved
for stated source classes) and no regularity of singular sources.

consumer_public_declarations.text:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, the convention of the
imported piecewise $C^1$ boundary and surface-measure definitions
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $U\cong I\times\Omega$ be the laboratory region
of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] with the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]]; let
$E,B$ be fields of [[def-em-fields]] and $\rho,J$ source fields of
[[def-em-sources]] on $\Omega\times I$; and let $(V,\nu_V)$ and $(D,r)$ be the
volume and patch test geometries of [[def-em-fixed-test-geometry]]. Assume the
fields are jointly $C^1$ on $\Omega\times I$ and that the additional
derivatives appearing below exist and are continuous there; for instance $E,B$
jointly of class $C^2$ and $\rho,J$ of class $C^1$ is sufficient.

(a) [Differential implies integral] If the smooth branch of
[[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] holds pointwise on $\Omega\times I$, then for every
volume test geometry $(V,\nu_V)$ and every $t\in I$,

$$\oint_{\partial V}E(\cdot,t)\cdot\nu_V\,dS=\frac{1}{\varepsilon_0}\int_V\rho(\cdot,t)\,d\lambda_3,\qquad \oint_{\partial V}B(\cdot,t)\cdot\nu_V\,dS=0,$$

and for every patch test geometry $(D,r)$ the flux functions
$t\mapsto\int_SB(\cdot,t)\cdot n_S\,dS$ and
$t\mapsto\int_SE(\cdot,t)\cdot n_S\,dS$ are differentiable on $I$ and, for
every $t\in I$,

$$\oint_{\partial S}E(\cdot,t)\cdot d\mathbf r=-\frac{d}{dt}\int_SB(\cdot,t)\cdot n_S\,dS,\qquad \oint_{\partial S}B(\cdot,t)\cdot d\mathbf r=\mu_0\int_SJ(\cdot,t)\cdot n_S\,dS+c^{-2}\frac{d}{dt}\int_SE(\cdot,t)\cdot n_S\,dS.$$

(b) [Integral implies differential] Conversely, suppose the two volume
identities of (a) hold for every volume test geometry and every $t\in I$, and
that for every patch test geometry the two flux functions are differentiable
on $I$ and the two patch identities of (a) hold for every $t\in I$. Then the
four smooth-branch equations of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] hold pointwise on
$\Omega\times I$:

$$\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0,\qquad \operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB,\qquad \operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE.$$

The equivalence is asserted for the exact class of test geometries of
[[def-em-fixed-test-geometry]], which contains the open interiors of all closed
axis-parallel boxes compactly contained in $\Omega$ and the affine square
patches; it is not a recovery from one selected volume or one selected patch,
and the divergence and curl of
[[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] and the time derivative of
[[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]] are the operators used.

supplier_public_sections.text:
**Set form.** Let $K\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be compact, Lebesgue measurable and of finite Lebesgue measure $\lambda_n(K)<\infty$, let $a<b$, and let $f$ be a real-valued function, defined and continuous together with its partial derivative $\partial_tf$ on an open neighbourhood of $K\times[a,b]$ in $\mathbb R^{n+1}$. Then $t\mapsto\int_Kf(x,t)\,d\lambda_n(x)$ is differentiable at every $t\in(a,b)$ with

$$\frac{d}{dt}\int_Kf(x,t)\,d\lambda_n(x)=\int_K\partial_tf(x,t)\,d\lambda_n(x),$$

and at $t=a$ and $t=b$ it has relative (one-sided) derivatives, taken within $[a,b]$, both equal to the same displayed integral. Equivalently, for every $t\in[a,b]$ and every sequence $h_k\to0$ with $h_k\ne0$ and $t+h_k\in[a,b]$,

$$\lim_{k\to\infty}\frac{1}{h_k}\Bigl(\int_Kf(x,t+h_k)\,d\lambda_n(x)-\int_Kf(x,t)\,d\lambda_n(x)\Bigr)=\int_K\partial_tf(x,t)\,d\lambda_n(x).$$

**Surface form.** Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, [[def-countable-choice]]) for the surface measure of [[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]]. Let $S$ be a fixed compact embedded $C^1$ hypersurface in $\mathbb R^m$, $m\ge2$, and let $f$ be real-valued, defined and continuous together with $\partial_tf$ on an open neighbourhood of $S\times[a,b]$. Then $t\mapsto\int_Sf(\sigma,t)\,dS(\sigma)$ is differentiable in the same relative sense with

$$\frac{d}{dt}\int_Sf(\sigma,t)\,dS(\sigma)=\int_S\partial_tf(\sigma,t)\,dS(\sigma).$$

The statements are pointwise in $t$ and make no claim about moving parameter sets $K(t)$ or $S(t)$, about singularities crossing $K$ or $S$, about differentiability of $\partial_tf$, or about differentiation in the spatial variables; only the one-dimensional parameter $t$ is differentiated. Integrals are Lebesgue integrals, and the surface integrals are those of the cited surface measure; the case $K=\varnothing$ or $\lambda_n(K)=0$ is included and the two sides vanish.

consumer_public_declarations.text:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, the convention of the
imported piecewise $C^1$ boundary and surface-measure definitions
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $U\cong I\times\Omega$ be the laboratory region
of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] with the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]]; let
$E,B$ be fields of [[def-em-fields]] and $\rho,J$ source fields of
[[def-em-sources]] on $\Omega\times I$; and let $(V,\nu_V)$ and $(D,r)$ be the
volume and patch test geometries of [[def-em-fixed-test-geometry]]. Assume the
fields are jointly $C^1$ on $\Omega\times I$ and that the additional
derivatives appearing below exist and are continuous there; for instance $E,B$
jointly of class $C^2$ and $\rho,J$ of class $C^1$ is sufficient.

(a) [Differential implies integral] If the smooth branch of
[[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] holds pointwise on $\Omega\times I$, then for every
volume test geometry $(V,\nu_V)$ and every $t\in I$,

$$\oint_{\partial V}E(\cdot,t)\cdot\nu_V\,dS=\frac{1}{\varepsilon_0}\int_V\rho(\cdot,t)\,d\lambda_3,\qquad \oint_{\partial V}B(\cdot,t)\cdot\nu_V\,dS=0,$$

and for every patch test geometry $(D,r)$ the flux functions
$t\mapsto\int_SB(\cdot,t)\cdot n_S\,dS$ and
$t\mapsto\int_SE(\cdot,t)\cdot n_S\,dS$ are differentiable on $I$ and, for
every $t\in I$,

$$\oint_{\partial S}E(\cdot,t)\cdot d\mathbf r=-\frac{d}{dt}\int_SB(\cdot,t)\cdot n_S\,dS,\qquad \oint_{\partial S}B(\cdot,t)\cdot d\mathbf r=\mu_0\int_SJ(\cdot,t)\cdot n_S\,dS+c^{-2}\frac{d}{dt}\int_SE(\cdot,t)\cdot n_S\,dS.$$

(b) [Integral implies differential] Conversely, suppose the two volume
identities of (a) hold for every volume test geometry and every $t\in I$, and
that for every patch test geometry the two flux functions are differentiable
on $I$ and the two patch identities of (a) hold for every $t\in I$. Then the
four smooth-branch equations of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] hold pointwise on
$\Omega\times I$:

$$\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0,\qquad \operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB,\qquad \operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE.$$

The equivalence is asserted for the exact class of test geometries of
[[def-em-fixed-test-geometry]], which contains the open interiors of all closed
axis-parallel boxes compactly contained in $\Omega$ and the affine square
patches; it is not a recovery from one selected volume or one selected patch,
and the divergence and curl of
[[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] and the time derivative of
[[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]] are the operators used.

consumer_facts.text:
[F7] If a parameter family of integrals has a continuous integrand with
continuous parameter derivative on a neighbourhood of a compact parameter set,
the integral is differentiable in the parameter with the derivative obtained
by differentiating under the integral ([[lem-em-parameter-integrals]]).

supplier_public_sections.text:
Adopt as a physical postulate of this framework the following four equations for
the fields of [[def-em-fields]] and the sources of [[def-em-sources]] on the
laboratory region $U\cong I\times\Omega$ of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], with
$\mu_0>0$, $c>0$, $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ and the SI units of
[[def-em-si-conventions]].

(a) [Smooth branch] Let $E,B$ be jointly $C^1$ fields with the additional
derivatives required by each equation existing and continuous, and let
$\rho,J$ be continuous. Then, with the divergence and curl of
[[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] and the partial derivative
$\partial_t$ at fixed position of
[[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]],

$$\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0,\qquad \operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB,\qquad \operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE.$$

(b) [Weak branch] Let instead $E,B$ be locally integrable $\mathbb R^3$-valued
fields and $\rho,J$ locally integrable scalar and vector fields on
$I\times\Omega$, identified with their regular distributions
([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]],
[[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]). Let
$\operatorname{div}$, $\operatorname{curl}$ and $\partial_t$ act as
distributional derivatives, componentwise, and let $\psi$ range over
$C_c^\infty(I\times\Omega)$ ([[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]]).
Then the same four identities hold in the sense of [[def-distribution]]: the
pairings

$$\langle\operatorname{div}E-\rho/\varepsilon_0,\psi\rangle,\qquad \langle\operatorname{div}B,\psi\rangle,\qquad \langle\operatorname{curl}E+\partial_tB,\psi\rangle,\qquad \langle\operatorname{curl}B-\mu_0J-c^{-2}\partial_tE,\psi\rangle$$

all vanish for every such $\psi$, all derivatives being distributional
derivatives ([[def-distributional-derivative]]).

(c) [Scope] The postulate contains no magnetic charge: $\operatorname{div}B=0$
and no magnetic-source term appears in $\operatorname{curl}E$. Sources that
are not locally integrable functions (point or sheet sources) are covered by
neither branch and require their own definition. The equations are adopted
classical vacuum physics in the named inertial chart; they are not deduced from
charge conservation, from empirical agreement or from the special-relativity
postulates, and this item by itself asserts no covariance under changes of
inertial frame.

consumer_public_declarations.text:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, the convention of the
imported piecewise $C^1$ boundary and surface-measure definitions
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $U\cong I\times\Omega$ be the laboratory region
of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] with the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]]; let
$E,B$ be fields of [[def-em-fields]] and $\rho,J$ source fields of
[[def-em-sources]] on $\Omega\times I$; and let $(V,\nu_V)$ and $(D,r)$ be the
volume and patch test geometries of [[def-em-fixed-test-geometry]]. Assume the
fields are jointly $C^1$ on $\Omega\times I$ and that the additional
derivatives appearing below exist and are continuous there; for instance $E,B$
jointly of class $C^2$ and $\rho,J$ of class $C^1$ is sufficient.

(a) [Differential implies integral] If the smooth branch of
[[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] holds pointwise on $\Omega\times I$, then for every
volume test geometry $(V,\nu_V)$ and every $t\in I$,

$$\oint_{\partial V}E(\cdot,t)\cdot\nu_V\,dS=\frac{1}{\varepsilon_0}\int_V\rho(\cdot,t)\,d\lambda_3,\qquad \oint_{\partial V}B(\cdot,t)\cdot\nu_V\,dS=0,$$

and for every patch test geometry $(D,r)$ the flux functions
$t\mapsto\int_SB(\cdot,t)\cdot n_S\,dS$ and
$t\mapsto\int_SE(\cdot,t)\cdot n_S\,dS$ are differentiable on $I$ and, for
every $t\in I$,

$$\oint_{\partial S}E(\cdot,t)\cdot d\mathbf r=-\frac{d}{dt}\int_SB(\cdot,t)\cdot n_S\,dS,\qquad \oint_{\partial S}B(\cdot,t)\cdot d\mathbf r=\mu_0\int_SJ(\cdot,t)\cdot n_S\,dS+c^{-2}\frac{d}{dt}\int_SE(\cdot,t)\cdot n_S\,dS.$$

(b) [Integral implies differential] Conversely, suppose the two volume
identities of (a) hold for every volume test geometry and every $t\in I$, and
that for every patch test geometry the two flux functions are differentiable
on $I$ and the two patch identities of (a) hold for every $t\in I$. Then the
four smooth-branch equations of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] hold pointwise on
$\Omega\times I$:

$$\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0,\qquad \operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB,\qquad \operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE.$$

The equivalence is asserted for the exact class of test geometries of
[[def-em-fixed-test-geometry]], which contains the open interiors of all closed
axis-parallel boxes compactly contained in $\Omega$ and the affine square
patches; it is not a recovery from one selected volume or one selected patch,
and the divergence and curl of
[[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] and the time derivative of
[[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]] are the operators used.

supplier_public_sections.text:
Let the laboratory region $U\cong I\times\Omega$, its spatial Euclidean structure
and its units be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] and
[[def-em-si-conventions]], and let $k\ge1$. An **electric field of class
$C^k$** on the region is a map $E:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ that is of class
$C^k$ in the sense of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]; a
**magnetic field of class $C^k$** is a map $B:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ of
the same class. At fixed $t\in I$ the maps $E(\cdot,t),B(\cdot,t):\Omega\to
\mathbb R^3$ are real spatial vector fields on the region $\Omega$, read in the
$\delta$-orthonormal basis $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of the frame. The framework uses:
$C^1$ fields in the classical Maxwell branch, $C^2$ fields where second or
mixed time-space derivatives of the fields appear, and $C^\infty$ fields in
the smooth existence branches; every statement carries its own regularity and
no regularity beyond it is asserted.

Conventions:

(a) $E$ is a **polar vector** and $B$ an **axial vector** relative to the
orientation of the spatial basis; the changes of inertial description adopted
for this framework are proper and orientation preserving, so
orientation-reversing descriptions are not among them.

(b) The fields are defined by their values on $\Omega\times I$, and no value at
a point of singular source support is asserted.

(c) $E$ carries V m$^{-1}$ and $B$ carries T.

(d) The identification of the pair $(E,B)$ with the components of an
alternating two-form, including its transformation behaviour, is made in the
framework's electromagnetic two-form definition on this page and is not
presupposed here.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, the convention of
the test-geometry and divergence-theorem items cited below
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $U\cong I\times\Omega$ be the laboratory
region of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] with the constants of
[[def-em-si-conventions]], and let $E,B$ be jointly of class $C^2$ fields of
[[def-em-fields]] and $\rho,J$ of class $C^1$ source fields of
[[def-em-sources]] satisfying the smooth branch of
[[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] on a neighbourhood of the data below.

Suppose given two patch test geometries $(D,r_1)$, $(D,r_2)$ of
[[def-em-fixed-test-geometry]] over the same finite elementary Green region
$D$ whose induced boundary chains coincide as oriented paths (so both patches
span the same closed loop $\gamma$), and suppose there is a bounded open
region $V\subseteq\Omega$ with a specified finite piecewise $C^1$ presentation
whose boundary faces are exactly the two images $r_1[D]$, $r_2[D]$ with
outward normals $-n_1$ and $+n_2$ respectively, where $n_i$ is the normal
induced by $r_i$ (that is, $V$ is the region enclosed between the two patches;
this is a hypothesis on the pair, part of its data). Then, for every $t\in I$:

(a) [Total current flux is surface independent]

$$\int_{S_1}\bigl(J+\varepsilon_0\partial_tE\bigr)(\cdot,t)\cdot n_1\,dS=\int_{S_2}\bigl(J+\varepsilon_0\partial_tE\bigr)(\cdot,t)\cdot n_2\,dS=\frac{1}{\mu_0}\oint_\gamma B(\cdot,t)\cdot d\mathbf r,$$

where $S_i=r_i[D]$ and the flux is that of
[[def-oriented-unit-normal-and-flux-of-a-surface-patch]].

(b) [Conduction-only flux need not be] For every $t\in I$ the difference of
the conduction fluxes equals the negative of the difference of the
displacement fluxes:

exact SI defining value $e=1.602\,176\,634\times10^{-19}\ \mathrm{C}$, and this
item does not assert that physical charge is quantised; the magnetic constant
$\mu_0>0$ carries N A$^{-2}$ and is measured, so no exact numerical value of

effect on 20 May 2019, $\mu_0$ is experimentally determined. The SI brochure

framework by

standard uncertainty of $\mu_0$.

charge density $\rho$ of the framework's source definition carries C m$^{-3}$
and the current density $J$ carries A m$^{-2}$, so that the four-current
components $(c\rho,J)$ carry A m$^{-2}$; the electric field $E$ carries
V m$^{-1}$; the magnetic field $B$ carries the tesla (T), where
$1\ \mathrm{T}=1\ \mathrm{N\,A^{-1}\,m^{-1}}$; the scalar potential $\varphi$
carries V and the vector potential $A$ carries T m, so that the four-potential
components $(\varphi/c,A)$ carry T m; the components of the electromagnetic
two-form of the framework's tensor definition carry T; a force carries the
newton (N), $1\ \mathrm{N}=1\ \mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-2}}$.

(kg) and a four-momentum $P=mU$ of the relativistic particle model carries

units; it does not show that a quantity is primitive in this or any other

themselves identify $c$ with the vacuum propagation constant of ideal light,

supplier_public_sections.text:
Let the laboratory region and its chart be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], with
the units of [[def-em-si-conventions]].

(a) [Charge parameter] The framework takes a real **charge parameter**
$q\in\mathbb R$, measured in coulombs, attached to a source; its sign is the
sign of the source and it is a parameter of the model. Charge quantisation is
not asserted.

(b) [Smooth source fields] A **smooth (volume) source field** on
$\Omega\times I$ is a pair $(\rho,J)$ of maps $\rho:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R$,
$J:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ that is continuous on $\Omega\times I$ and of
class $C^1$ wherever a displayed equation differentiates it; $\rho$ is the
**frame charge density** (C m$^{-3}$) and $J$ the **frame current density**
(A m$^{-2}$). For each fixed $t\in I$ retain the compact Jordan branch: if
$V\subseteq\Omega$ is compact and Jordan measurable, define

$$Q_R(V,t):=\int_V\rho(y,t)dy$$

by [[def-riemann-integral-over-a-jordan-set]], with integrability supplied by
[[thm-continuous-functions-on-compact-jordan-sets-are-integrable]]. For the
full measurable-volume branch assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]),
as required by the published Lebesgue-measure interface. If $V$ is any bounded
Lebesgue-measurable subset with compact closure $\overline V\subseteq\Omega$,
define

$$Q(V,t):=\int_V\rho(y,t)d\lambda_3(y)=\int_{\mathbb R^3}F_t(y)\mathbf{1}_V(y)d\lambda_3(y),$$

where $F_t=\rho(\cdot,t)$ on $\Omega$ and $0$ elsewhere; the signed integral is
defined through its positive and negative parts
([[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]],
[[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]]). The
function $F_t$ is Borel, and hence Lebesgue measurable: for every open
$O\subseteq\mathbb R$ its preimage inside the open set $\Omega$ is relatively
open in $\Omega$, hence open in $\mathbb R^3$, and the closed complement of
$\Omega$ is added precisely when $0\in O$
([[thm-continuous-preimages-of-borel-sets-are-borel]],
[[thm-borel-sets-are-lebesgue-measurable]]). This integral is absolutely
finite: $\rho(\cdot,t)$ is bounded on the compact $\overline V$ by
[[thm-extreme-value-metric]], $V$ has finite Lebesgue measure by
[[prop-lebesgue-measure-is-sigma-finite-and-finite-on-bounded-sets]], and the
monotonicity and homogeneity of the nonnegative integral
([[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]) bound
$\int|F_t|\mathbf{1}_Vd\lambda_3\le M_t\lambda_3(V)<\infty$, the indicator
integral being its simple-function value
([[prop-the-nonnegative-integral-agrees-with-the-simple-integral]]); the
positive and negative parts are measurable by
[[prop-closure-properties-of-measurable-functions-used-by-the-integral]]. On
the compact Jordan branch, under the same Countable Choice assumption,
$Q=Q_R$ by [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]].
The
empty region has charge zero in both branches. The current flux remains
defined independently: for each oriented surface patch in $\Omega$ the current
flux at time $t$ is the surface integral of $J(\cdot,t)$ in the induced
orientation, as defined in [[def-oriented-unit-normal-and-flux-of-a-surface-patch]].
Point sources and sheet sources are not source fields in this sense; they are
different objects, defined by their own pairings when the framework uses them.

(c) [Covariant identification] Write $j:=(c\rho,J)$, so $j^0=c\rho$ and
$j^i=J^i$. The framework adopts as a model premise the identification of the
charge-current of a source with a vector field of the affine Minkowski model,
and hence the component transformation law of
[[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] for $j$ between inertial charts.
This is a model premise, not a theorem about physical currents.

(d) [Frame density, scalar multiplier and the normalized material branch]
Suppose additionally that the identified $j$ is $C^1$ and $j=\rho_0U$, with a
$C^1$ future timelike vector field $U$ and a $C^1$ real scalar multiplier
$\rho_0$. Since $U^0>0$, define the normalized chart direction $u:=U/U^0$, so
$u^0=1$, $u^i=U^i/U^0$. Then $j=(\rho_0U^0)u$ and, because the electromagnetic
convention is $j^0=c\rho$,

$$\rho=\rho_0U^0/c,\qquad J^i=\rho_0U^i=c\rho\,u^i.$$

Pointwise equality $\rho=\rho_0$ holds if and only if $\rho_0(U^0-c)=0$,
including the zero-multiplier case. Where $\rho_0\ne0$, equality is equivalent
to $U^0=c$, which does not alone imply $U^i=0$ for an arbitrary future timelike
$U$. Thus a scalar multiplier is not automatically a Lorentz rest charge
density. The direction $u$ is chart normalized, with no unit or
proper-four-velocity normalization imposed in this general branch; if its
coordinate velocity interpretation is adopted, the spatial velocity is
$v^i:=cu^i$.

For the separate convective source model, explicitly assume that $U$ is the
material proper-time four-velocity, normalized by $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$ as in
[[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]. This is an additional model
condition, not a consequence of the factorization $j=\rho_0U$. In that branch,
$U=\gamma(c,v)$, $|v|<c$, $\gamma=(1-|v|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$, and

$$\rho=\gamma\rho_0,\qquad J=\rho v.$$

Here $\rho_0$ is the rest charge density of this stipulated convective model:
in a comoving inertial frame $U=(c,0,0,0)$ and $j=(c\rho_0,0,0,0)$. The
equality $\rho=\rho_0$ then holds exactly where $\rho_0=0$ or $v=0$
(equivalently $\gamma=1$). Both signs of charge and the zero-density case are
retained.

(e) [Scope] This definition fixes the source objects of the smooth branch and
their transformation interface. It asserts no conservation law (that is proved
for stated source classes) and no regularity of singular sources.

consumer_public_declarations.text:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, the convention of
the test-geometry and divergence-theorem items cited below
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $U\cong I\times\Omega$ be the laboratory
region of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] with the constants of
[[def-em-si-conventions]], and let $E,B$ be jointly of class $C^2$ fields of
[[def-em-fields]] and $\rho,J$ of class $C^1$ source fields of
[[def-em-sources]] satisfying the smooth branch of
[[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] on a neighbourhood of the data below.

Suppose given two patch test geometries $(D,r_1)$, $(D,r_2)$ of
[[def-em-fixed-test-geometry]] over the same finite elementary Green region
$D$ whose induced boundary chains coincide as oriented paths (so both patches
span the same closed loop $\gamma$), and suppose there is a bounded open
region $V\subseteq\Omega$ with a specified finite piecewise $C^1$ presentation
whose boundary faces are exactly the two images $r_1[D]$, $r_2[D]$ with
outward normals $-n_1$ and $+n_2$ respectively, where $n_i$ is the normal
induced by $r_i$ (that is, $V$ is the region enclosed between the two patches;
this is a hypothesis on the pair, part of its data). Then, for every $t\in I$:

(a) [Total current flux is surface independent]

$$\int_{S_1}\bigl(J+\varepsilon_0\partial_tE\bigr)(\cdot,t)\cdot n_1\,dS=\int_{S_2}\bigl(J+\varepsilon_0\partial_tE\bigr)(\cdot,t)\cdot n_2\,dS=\frac{1}{\mu_0}\oint_\gamma B(\cdot,t)\cdot d\mathbf r,$$

where $S_i=r_i[D]$ and the flux is that of
[[def-oriented-unit-normal-and-flux-of-a-surface-patch]].

(b) [Conduction-only flux need not be] For every $t\in I$ the difference of
the conduction fluxes equals the negative of the difference of the
displacement fluxes:

$$\int_{S_1}J(\cdot,t)\cdot n_1\,dS-\int_{S_2}J(\cdot,t)\cdot n_2\,dS=-\varepsilon_0\left(\int_{S_1}\partial_tE(\cdot,t)\cdot n_1\,dS-\int_{S_2}\partial_tE(\cdot,t)\cdot n_2\,dS\right).$$

Hence the conduction-only fluxes are equal exactly when the displacement
fluxes are equal, and neither conclusion is forced by the Maxwell equations
alone.

(c) [Explicit realisation] The following declared smooth data satisfies all
the hypotheses above and has different conduction fluxes through the two
surfaces. On $\Omega=\mathbb R^3$, $I=\mathbb R$, fix $\chi\in C^\infty(\mathbb
R)$ with $0\le\chi\le1$, $\chi(z)=1$ for $z\le-1$ and $\chi(z)=0$ for
$z\ge0$, and set

$$E(x,t):=\frac{t}{\varepsilon_0}\chi(z)\,e_z,\qquad B:=0,\qquad \rho(x,t):=t\,\chi'(z),\qquad J(x,t):=-\chi(z)\,e_z.$$

Then $\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0$, $\operatorname{div}B=0$,
$\operatorname{curl}E=0=-\partial_tB$,
$\operatorname{curl}B=0=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$ (the last identity because
$c^{-2}\varepsilon_0^{-1}=\mu_0$), and $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$.
Take $D=[-1,1]^2$ and its interior $D^\circ=(-1,1)^2$. Let $\sigma$ be the
standard smooth step of [[def-the-standard-smooth-step-function]] and define
$h(s):=\sigma(2(1-s^2))$, $\eta(u,v):=h(u)h(v)$. Then
$\eta\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^2)$, $0\le\eta\le1$, $\eta=1$ in a
neighbourhood of the origin, $\eta>0$ at every point of $D^\circ$, and $\eta=0$
on $\partial D$ and outside $D$. Take the graphs

$$r_1(u,v):=(u,v,-2\eta(u,v)),\qquad r_2(u,v):=(u,v,0).$$

Both induced boundary chains are the square
$\{(u,v,0):(u,v)\in\partial D\}$, the region
$V=\{(u,v,w):(u,v)\in D^\circ,\ -2\eta(u,v)<w<0\}$ is enclosed between the
patches, and

$$\int_{S_1}J\cdot n_1\,dS=-\int_D\chi(-2\eta(u,v))\,dudv<0,\qquad \int_{S_2}J\cdot n_2\,dS=-\int_D\chi(0)\,dudv=0,$$

the first inequality because $\eta=1$ in a neighbourhood of the origin, so
$\chi(-2\eta)=1$ on a nonempty open subset of $D$, whose area is positive,
while both total current fluxes in (a) vanish, consistently with the loop
integral $\oint_\gamma B\cdot d\mathbf r=0$. In the standard
charging-capacitor discussion the two spanning surfaces cut the conduction
current in different ways and the difference is carried by the displacement
term; the realisation above exhibits exactly this phenomenon in a
self-contained smooth model. An idealised thin-wire current is not a source
type of this framework and the capacitor interpretation is explanatory, not
an additional empirical claim.
